claims.author: alexanderwiederin
claims.question: whether multi-threaded applications are supported and desired
claims.quote: Does this support multi-threaded applications? If not, do we want it to?

status_by.quote: It should be thread-safe, but I don't think this is particularly interesting to run in a multi-threaded context.

claims.status_note: author explained thread safety and that multithreading is not the main use case

claims.author: alexanderwiederin
claims.question: whether a CI job is needed to run with ENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE=ON
claims.quote: Do we need a CI job to run with `ENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE=ON`?

status_by.quote: I wasn't sure where to put such a job, so I didn't introduce it here.

claims.status_note: author replied unsure where to put it and questioned if worthwhile yet

claims.author: alexanderwiederin
claims.quote: I think we have to define what each code means. What do you think?
claims.request: define what each error code means

status_by.quote: I think we should leave this here - it's fairly straight forward to get the error code header from somewhere. I'll try to open another pull request

claims.status_note: author replied preferring to expose the error list in a follow-up PR

claims.author: alexanderwiederin
claims.quote: Could `ScriptTraceScope` snapshot the callback in its constructor? That takes both the mutex acquisition and the std::function copy out of the per-opcode path.
claims.request: snapshot the callback in ScriptTraceScope's constructor to take mutex acquisition and std::function copy out of per-opcode path

status_by.quote: Done.

claims.status_note: author implemented callback snapshotting in constructor

claims.author: elmeriniemela
claims.question: whether it is expected that a trace can be invalid while the script error code is OK
claims.quote: one weirdness that I found is that a trace can be invalid, but the related script error code is still OK.

status_by.quote: What you are seeing is the intended behaviour here. Your LLM seems to already have inferred the correct scenario from the context.

claims.status_note: author explained this is expected because EvalScript does not enforce final stack conditions

claims.author: haanhvu
claims.quote: Should we clearly comment that user data is destroyed in any case, whether tracing enabled/succeeds or not, to avoid problems like double free?
claims.request: add a comment that user data is destroyed in any case to avoid problems like double free

status_by.quote: I don't think this needs an extra comment. To me it seems self-explanatory.

claims.status_note: author declined, viewing it as self-explanatory

claims.author: haanhvu
claims.harm: BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL on vector size allows test execution to continue and access out-of-bounds indices, causing undefined behavior
claims.quote: BOOST_CHECK_EQUAL(states.size(), 11) is non-fatal, but the test checks states[0] through states[10] after this. So if the size check fails, the test still continues and may access out-of-bound items,

status_by.quote: made the boost size check a hard requirement.

claims.status_note: author fixed by making boost size check a hard requirement

claims.author: haanhvu
claims.quote: Should we verify unregistering actually stops tracing?
claims.request: verify that unregistering the tracer actually stops tracing

status_by.quote: added a quick verification that unregistering the tracer actually works.

claims.status_note: author added verification that unregistering works

claims.author: haanhvu
claims.quote: Nit: `state` is already passed by value here, so `m_state.emplace_back(state)` performs an extra copy of the `ScriptTraceFrame`. Would it make sense to move it instead?
claims.request: std::move state into m_state to avoid an extra copy of ScriptTraceFrame

status_by.quote: I don't think this matters in a test. Besides, the new type is hardly worth the move now.

claims.status_note: author declined as not mattering for a test

claims.author: haanhvu
claims.quote: Should we extend the test to cover this callback replacement contract?
claims.request: extend tests to cover callback replacement contract

status_by.quote: added a verification that re-registering the tracer works.

claims.status_note: author added test verification that re-registering the tracer works

claims.author: stringintech
claims.quote: would it make sense to make the frame opaque like other `btck_*` types, with getters, instead of a public struct
claims.request: make frame opaque with getters instead of a public struct

status_by.quote: wrapped the frame into nested opaque types and getters.

claims.status_note: author wrapped the frame into nested opaque types and getters

claims.author: stringintech
claims.quote: Perhaps it is better to use an exhaustive switch for `kind` and `sig_version` as well, in both directions
claims.request: use exhaustive switch for kind and sig_version conversions

status_by.quote: use exhaustive enum conversions.

claims.status_note: author switched to exhaustive enum conversions

claims.quote: can we drop the closure and give it a fixed dummy in begin and end frames?
claims.request: drop the closure for f_exec and use a fixed dummy in begin and end frames

status_by.quote: dropped f_exec pre-loading with a lambda. As suggested, the begin and end frames now contain dummy values

claims.status_note: author dropped f_exec preloading closure and documented dummy values in begin and end frames

status_by.quote: I'm not sure if this is still relevant after the last push. In any case, I don't want the tests here to be exhaustive.

claims.status_note: author declined making tests exhaustive

claims.harm: EvalScript triggers an assertion failure when tracing is enabled if called with a null serror pointer (e.g. in CheckSignetBlockSolution)
claims.quote: The tracing code assumes serror is non-null whenever a callback is registered, but EvalScript permits nullptr... This triggers the assertion assert(!m_callback || error);

status_by.quote: making the error code "optional" by encoding `-1` as a nullopt. This gets rid of the assertion

claims.status_note: author pushed fix making error code optional instead of asserting

claims.harm: oversized scripts are rejected before ScriptTraceScope is instantiated, preventing BEGIN and END trace frames from being emitted
claims.quote: EvalScript rejects oversized scripts before constructing ScriptTraceScope, so a registered callback receives neither BEGIN nor END.

claims.status_note: author declined changing interpreter and noted kernel lib catches the length check
